fact_rationales.F12: Single S2 and systolic ejection murmur are more typical of conditions with abnormal right ventricular outflow, such as Tricuspid Atresia or Double Outlet Right Ventricle, rather than Tetralogy of Fallot which typically presents with a harsh systolic ejection murmur due to right ventricular outflow tract obstruction.
fact_rationales.F15: Enlarged cardiac silhouette with increased pulmonary vasculature is more suggestive of conditions with increased pulmonary blood flow, such as Tricuspid Atresia or Double Outlet Right Ventricle, rather than Tetralogy of Fallot which typically presents with decreased pulmonary blood flow.

fact_rationales.F11: Nasal flaring, costosternal retractions, and perioral cyanosis are signs of respiratory distress, which can be seen in several cardiac anomalies, but are particularly common in transposition of the great arteries and total anomalous pulmonary venous connection.
fact_rationales.F12: A single S2 and systolic ejection murmur can be heard in several cardiac anomalies, but the presence of a single S2 is more characteristic of transposition of the great arteries and truncus arteriosus.
fact_rationales.F15: An enlarged cardiac silhouette with increased pulmonary vasculature can be seen in several cardiac anomalies, but is particularly common in transposition of the great arteries, total anomalous pulmonary venous connection, and truncus arteriosus.
fact_rationales.F9: Tachycardia is a common finding in various cardiac anomalies, but truncus arteriosus may have a more pronounced effect on heart rate due to the single common ventricular outflow tract.
